subject: biology
title: Animal and plant cell structures
key_idea: Animal and plant cells contain sub-cellular structures, and each one has a job. Plant cells also have a cell wall, a permanent vacuole and (often) chloroplasts. You must be able to link each structure to its function.

blocks.text: Most animal cells have the same five parts. This section covers what each part does.

items.meaning: A part inside a cell that has a job to do.
The jelly-like liquid that fills the cell.
The reaction that releases energy for the cell to use.

rows: Contains the genetic material (DNA in chromosomes) and controls the activities of the cell
Controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell
Where aerobic respiration happens, which releases energy

diagram.alt: Tap each cell structure to see what it does, then test yourself on matching structures to functions. The structures are the nucleus, cytoplasm, cell membrane, mitochondria, ribosomes, chloroplasts, permanent vacuole and cell wall.
diagram.prompt: Structures of animal and plant cells

parts.name: Nucleus
parts.detail: Contains the genetic material and controls the activities of the cell.

parts.name: Cytoplasm
parts.detail: A jelly-like liquid where most chemical reactions happen.

parts.name: Cell membrane
parts.detail: Controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.

parts.name: Mitochondria
parts.detail: Where aerobic respiration happens, which releases energy.

parts.name: Ribosomes
parts.detail: Where protein synthesis happens: this is where proteins are made.

parts.name: Chloroplasts
parts.detail: Contain chlorophyll, which absorbs light for photosynthesis. Found in some plant cells only.

parts.name: Permanent vacuole
parts.detail: Filled with cell sap. Found in plant cells only.

parts.name: Cell wall
parts.detail: Made of cellulose. Strengthens the cell. Found in plant and algal cells.

items: The nucleus controls the cell. It contains the DNA.
Mitochondria release energy by aerobic respiration.
The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves. Ribosomes make proteins.

blocks.text: Plant cells have all the animal cell parts, plus three more. Algal cells have them too.

rows: Contain chlorophyll, which absorbs light for photosynthesis
Made of cellulose. Strengthens the cell

blocks.text: Not every plant cell is the same

items: Root cells are underground, so they get no light and have **no chloroplasts**.
Leaf cells that photosynthesise have many chloroplasts.
A green colour in a cell or stem comes from chlorophyll in the chloroplasts.

diagram.alt: A table comparing animal and plant cells. Both have a nucleus, cytoplasm, cell membrane, mitochondria and ribosomes. Only plant cells have a cell wall, a permanent vacuole and chloroplasts.
items: Animal cell
Plant cell
Plant cells have a cell wall, a permanent vacuole and chloroplasts. Animal cells do not.
The cell wall strengthens the cell. The cell membrane is not the same thing.
Chloroplasts are for photosynthesis, so cells in the dark have none.

blocks.text: A cell's structures match its job. Exam questions ask you to explain why a cell has a lot of one structure, or none.

items: Cells that need a lot of energy, such as heart muscle cells, contain **many mitochondria**.
More mitochondria means more respiration, which releases more energy for the muscle to contract.
Cells that make a lot of protein need **many ribosomes**.
Some cells have no nucleus, such as red blood cells and xylem cells.
Say mitochondria **release** energy. Energy is never made, produced or created.
Chlorophyll is a chemical, not a structure. The structure is the chloroplast.
Plasmids are small rings of DNA found in bacterial cells, not animal or plant cells.
Many mitochondria means a high demand for energy.
Link structure, process and result: more mitochondria, more respiration, more energy released.
Say "release" energy, never "make" energy.

checks.q: Name the part of a cell that controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.
Name two structures found in a plant cell but not in an animal cell.
checks.a: Any two from: cell wall, permanent vacuole, chloroplasts.

checks.q: Explain why a sperm cell or a muscle cell contains many mitochondria.
checks.a: More respiration happens in the mitochondria, which releases more energy. The cell needs the energy to move or contract.

worked_example.question: The heart is an organ that pumps blood around the body. Heart muscle cells contain many mitochondria. Explain why heart muscle cells contain many mitochondria.
answer_points: More respiration happens in the mitochondria.
Respiration releases more energy (or the muscle needs more energy).
So the heart muscle can contract.
worked_example.tip: Do not write that energy is produced, made or created, and do not write anaerobic respiration.

worked_example.question: The cytoplasm of a cell contains a nucleus. Explain the role of one other structure in the cytoplasm of a human cell.
answer_points: Mitochondria, which release energy (or are where respiration occurs).
OR ribosomes, which are where proteins are made (protein synthesis).
worked_example.tip: One mark for naming the structure and one for its role, and the role must match the structure you named.

worked_example.question: Cells contain structures that have different features. Complete the table using structures from this list: cell membrane, chloroplast, mitochondria, nucleus, ribosomes. The features are: (1) contains chlorophyll for photosynthesis, (2) contains enzymes for respiration, (3) has receptor molecules for communication.
answer_points: Has receptor molecules for communication: cell membrane.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each correct structure. Two structures in the list are not needed.

items: The cell membrane has **receptor molecules**, which let the cell communicate with other cells.
Mitochondria contain the **enzymes** needed for respiration.
Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which absorbs light for photosynthesis.

worked_example.question: Describe differences and similarities between the structure of a plant root hair cell and a bacterial cell.
answer_points: Differences (maximum 3): the root hair cell has a nucleus, mitochondria and a large permanent vacuole.
The root hair cell wall is made of cellulose.
The root hair cell has linear DNA and no plasmids.
Similarities (maximum 3): both have a cell wall, a cell membrane and cytoplasm.
Both have ribosomes and DNA (genetic material).
Five marks in total from the differences and similarities.
worked_example.tip: Give at least two similarities as well as differences, because the marks are shared between both.

worked_example.question: State the role of the cell membrane.
answer_points: It controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.
